q: Does a servo press use less electricity than a mechanical power press?
title: Servo vs mechanical power press
short: Usually yes. A mechanical press keeps a heavy flywheel spinning between strokes, so its motor draws power even when idle. A servo press draws power mainly during the stroke. The saving is largest where presses wait between parts. Meter kWh per thousand parts on both before deciding.
audience: Sheet metal and auto component press shops

ul: kWh per shift from a clamp meter or sub-meter.
Parts produced in the same shift.

p: Servo presses can cut scrap and die wear with better stroke control, which also lowers the material footprint per good part.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.
